task:
Set operation chains ignore the precedence rules of each SQL dialect. In standard SQL, INTERSECT binds tighter than UNION and EXCEPT. sqlglot parses every chain as flat and left-associative, so transpiling changes query results. Fix the parsing and generation so the grouping survives.

The rule: sqlglot's default dialect, Postgres, Spark and ClickHouse use INTERSECT-binds-tighter. Oracle, SQLite and Hive give all set operations equal precedence, left to right. The grouping must be explicit in the output, with parentheses, when a chain moves between dialects. Below, 'default' means generating with no dialect.

Reading as Postgres or Spark, SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3 must generate SELECT 1 UNION (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3). Reading as Postgres, SELECT 1 EXCEPT SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3 INTERSECT SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5 must generate SELECT 1 EXCEPT (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3 INTERSECT SELECT 4) UNION SELECT 5.

Reading as Oracle, SQLite or Hive, SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3 must generate (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2) INTERSECT SELECT 3.

A leading INTERSECT run needs no parentheses: SELECT 1 INTERSECT SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 stays unchanged reading as Oracle or Postgres.

Trailing modifiers belong to the outermost set operation. Reading as Postgres, SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 10 OFFSET 2 generates, in default, SELECT 1 UNION (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3) ORDER BY 1 NULLS LAST LIMIT 10 OFFSET 2. Reading as Postgres, SELECT (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3 ORDER BY 1) generates, in default, SELECT (SELECT 1 UNION (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3) ORDER BY 1 NULLS LAST). Generating that same query for Postgres gives SELECT (SELECT 1 UNION (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3) ORDER BY 1).

Modifiers placed after a parenthesized final operand also go on the whole set operation, as in SELECT 1 UNION (SELECT 2) ORDER BY 1.

Generating for SQLite, which does not accept parenthesized operands. Right grouping needs a wrapper: SELECT 1 UNION (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3) becomes SELECT 1 UNION SELECT * FROM (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3). Left grouping is implicit, so no wrapper is written: (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2) INTERSECT SELECT 3 becomes SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3. Comments on the dropped parentheses are kept: (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2) /* keep */ INTERSECT SELECT 3 becomes SELECT 1 /* keep */ UNION SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3. Doubled parentheses drop too, and duplicate column names are not renamed: ((SELECT 1 AS x, 2 AS x UNION SELECT 3, 4)) INTERSECT SELECT 1, 2 becomes SELECT 1 AS x, 2 AS x UNION SELECT 3, 4 INTERSECT SELECT 1, 2. A parenthesized left operand that has its own CTEs or query modifiers must keep its wrapper. Postgres and Oracle output of these parenthesized forms stays as written, and reading them as Postgres or Oracle keeps them unchanged.

ClickHouse. The FORMAT and SETTINGS clauses attach to the outer set operation, while LIMIT stays with the last operand. SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 2 FORMAT JSON becomes SELECT 1 UNION ALL (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 2) FORMAT JSON. SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 INTERSECT SELECT 1 LIMIT 1 SETTINGS limit = 1 becomes SELECT 1 UNION ALL (SELECT 1 INTERSECT SELECT 1 LIMIT 1) SETTINGS limit = 1. SELECT * FROM x LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM y stays unchanged.

Long chains must not hit the recursion limit. With sql = 'SELECT 1' + ' UNION SELECT 1 INTERSECT SELECT 1' * 200, parse_one(sql, read='hive').sql('postgres') must give the fully nested form, built by starting with 'SELECT 1' and repeating 200 times: expected = f'({expected} UNION SELECT 1) INTERSECT SELECT 1'. Scope building must cope as well. With 1000 repetitions read as Hive, len(list(build_scope(chain).traverse())) must be 4001.

Scopes must descend parenthesized operands correctly. For build_scope(parse_one('SELECT 1 UNION (SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3)')), the set_operation_scopes of the root, as scope.expression.sql(), must be ['SELECT 1', 'SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 3'].

Tolerant parsing must not produce a stray closing parenthesis: parse_one('SELECT 1 UNION', error_level=ErrorLevel.IGNORE).sql() must be 'SELECT 1 UNION'.

Pretty output must indent nested groupings. With pretty=True, ((SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2) INTERSECT SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4) INTERSECT SELECT 5 must give, with two-space indents per level:

(
  (
    SELECT
      1
    UNION
    SELECT
      2
  )
  INTERSECT
  SELECT
    3
  UNION
  SELECT
    4
)
INTERSECT
SELECT
  5

Everything else must keep working.
